title: John Henry in the age of AI
excerpt: John Henry raced a steam drill and won. And it changed nothing. My take, as a software engineer, on the old American folk tale, and what it gets right about facing down a machine built to replace you.
content_html:
There is an American folk tale about a man named John Henry. It dates to the mid 19th century, a time during which America was rapidly industrializing and the use of steam power was picking up… Well, steam.

Being a folklore tale, there are many different variations of it, though, most examples describe him as a man employed on the construction of railroads. His specific role is often described as a “steel-driving” man but this takes various specific forms such as hammering steel drills into rock to dig railroad tunnels, or hammering the spikes that hold the rails to the wooden sleepers. Generally speaking, John Henry is depicted as an extremely skilled and well respected worker.

There are many full-text versions available online, but I’ll specifically reference this one. The synopsis of the tale of John Henry is as follows:

  • John Henry is a railway construction worker and sees a steam-powered machine performing his job at an incredible pace.
  • He decides to measure his prowess as a railway construction worker by having a duel against the steam-powered machine. The duel is usually something along the lines of racing to mine a railway tunnel or set and spike down a length of track, with the winner being the fastest to complete.
  • John Henry ultimately beats the machine, but the exertion he put his body through to do so causes it to give out, and he passes away.

It is the classical man-versus-machine tale. And I think the parallels that can be drawn between it and the emergence of AI in recent years are clear, and I will discuss them later on.

I heard the story of John Henry when I was a child, but I forgot all about it until just recently. I subscribe to several different interpretations of the folklore tale, but, in my opinion, it ultimately boils down to a statement on how ever-advancing technology disrupts and conflicts with human dignity, perseverance, ability, and purpose. It is a reasonable conclusion that John Henry felt threatened by the emergence of technology that could replace him. And his response of setting up a duel against said technology suggests that he wanted to prove that he, a human, can equal or defeat the machine. And the outcome of the duel asserts that man, the human spirit, ultimately triumphs over machine, but at a cost. This time, the cost was John Henry’s life.

Looking back on this story almost two centuries later, with a modern perspective over the technology we have now, coaxes out some obviosities. The use of machinery in tunneling and railway construction are the norm. Construction without machinery and with only human labor is practically non-existent anywhere machinery is available. There are still “steel-driving” men, but their tools are no longer hand tools like John Henry’s, but machines.

And the benefits of this shift to mechanization are obvious: such projects are completed faster, consuming fewer resources, and - most importantly - more safely and with a lower human cost. Other external factors like safety standards evolving over time too absolutely come into play here. However, having fewer humans on the job site, and more machines, ultimately expose less humans to harm for simple mathematical reasons.

I assert that the meaning behind the tale of John Henry is directly applicable to what is happening right now. It can easily be interpreted as an allegory describing the emergence of AI and the impact that AI’s emergence has on how labor is executed and what the value of a human being is with respect to work.

Let’s interpret the tale of John Henry in the context of the last couple of years of technological advancement and the emergence and adoption of - and opposition to - AI. I’m a software engineer, and will largely speak from the perspective of my career.

Software engineering is a field some speculate will be replaced by AI. Boris Cherny is the creator and head of Claude Code at Anthropic and, Anthropic is currently one of the top companies that actually creates AI, rather than consuming it. Cherny famously stated that “coding is largely solved” - to the chagrin of many software engineers everywhere.

That’s our first parallel to John Henry. A machine has been created that, in theory, can take the place of a human and do a task a human was previously required for. This corresponds to the steam-powered machine John Henry dueled against.

Sidebar: I completely understand that you can’t remove a human from their desk and plop an AI there and get 1:1 results. I am not making the argument that AI is sophisticated and accurate enough that this is doable. I write code for a living. I have seen the code that AI generates. They are not on the same level yet. Yet. I am also not commenting on whether I think AI will ever reach that point. It is inarguable that technology advances and gets better, but it is not a given that all technologies advance and get better. Plenty hit their limit and do not evolve further.

Let’s get back to our steam and silicon powered machines.1 Watching the emergence of AI, I have absolutely felt the threat of it, personally. Watching a machine in seconds churn out a Python script that would have taken me at least an hour to write is frightening. Why pay me to spend an hour doing that when a machine can do it instantly? It felt like looking at my replacement. And I can imagine that John Henry, nearly two centuries ago, felt the same dread looking at the steam-powered machine doing his job.

How would my story look if I decided to duel the machine replacing me, like John Henry dueled his?

I’ve been programming since the mid 2000s, and professionally since 2010. I have always followed emerging technology, including AI, and looked for ways that I could leverage them to be a better developer. By now, I have a decent amount of experience using AI tools to execute my craft.

That being said, I look at the output of AI tools regularly and I have observed that it generally does not compare to code written by skilled humans. But that is not too surprising. Communicating the requirements of a software project often trips up humans too. There is an entire field of work dedicated to communicating and tracking requirements - project management. So it comes as no surprise that a bot lacking context outputs code that misses the mark. On top of that, AI is technologically limited by constraints like context windows that can easily lead to similar breakdowns.

But I also recognize that the code LLMs output is often “good enough”. It completes the task, but is written with patterns I don’t agree with or know better approaches to. And sometimes, that’s okay. The output can serve as a general skeleton, ready for improvements by humans. It can make assumptions that even a human missed, and now needs to consider. Or if the task is trivial enough, say one-off tasks, “good enough” might just be good enough.

I also need to mention that sometimes AI writes code exactly as I would have written it, which feels amazing and magical.

Quality does matter to me. I cannot stress enough how much it pains me to ship ugly, but working, code. Even outside the context of AI. I fully recognize Steve Jobs to be a deeply flawed man, but I adore the story of his interaction with his father in which his father explains the value of a job done right and with care.

The story of John Henry doesn’t touch on the quality of the work or whether it mattered to him. But, his position on the matter can be inferred. Versions of the tale include:

He picked up a hammer and a little piece of steel

Saying, “Hammer’s going to be the death of me, Lord, Lord,

    Hammer’s going to be the death of me.”

John Henry dedicated his life to his craft.

And that brings us to the crux of what I’m trying to convey:

He cared about the craft and pride of the work itself, not just the outcome. And the same is true when it comes to AI: If you care about making and doing, and the process is more important than the result, AI isn’t for you.

If you’re trying to get a job done, AI can be a force multiplier. The code might not be great, but it just might work. Human code needs review and tweaking, and that doesn’t go away with AI. Human-written code can still be slop and that slop can get sent to production if it goes unreviewed.

These are the two extremes. The far, far ends of the spectrum of AI use. What defines the reasonable middle ground?

Quality defines the middle ground. A skilled developer can use AI as a force multiplier to write more code at the same quality he would have otherwise, but faster. And that’s what I think a major part of the debate around AI is. What I’ve revealed here is that it all boils down to what one’s viewpoint of the purpose of a human being is.

Everybody has to work to make the world and society go around. A lot of people think this sucks, and working your entire life is a tragedy. And I’m inclined to agree.

But I also see technology as an escape from this existence. In John Henry’s time, digging a tunnel required the toil of thousands of men and women. Or, similarly, farming required hundreds of men or women working the fields, becoming sunburnt and ruining their backs bending down to reach the plants on the ground. These occupations were dangerous and took an extreme toll on the body.

But those jobs are done differently now. Farming no longer requires thousands tending the fields year-round, almost all of the work can be done by machine, with one machine replacing many, many workers. Ditto for tunneling.

The men and women that would have been dying or destroying their bodies doing such labor are now doing something else. That something else might not take a similar toll on their body. And that’s a good thing. I’m describing a net reduction human suffering. And I’m describing manpower that has been freed up that can now be put towards something else that improves humanity, like figuring out how to replace jobs that are necessary but incur human suffering with solutions and machines that don’t suffer.

However, it’s worth mentioning that shift doesn’t happen overnight. People out of work because they were replaced by automation can have a hard time finding a new job. Starting over and shifting to a new field of work is often necessary due to the very automation making the job market in a specific field disappear. Some people become poorer. There are immediate and real world consequences worth considering. This is a legitimate grievance.

But, machines replacing humans isn’t inherently a bad thing. It can be beneficial as it frees up labor resources - those humans - and potentially allocates them to fields that advances the knowledge and capabilities and comfort of the human race.

And it’s a snowball effect. The observation that technology is advancing at a faster and faster pace is a common one, and accurate in my opinion.

I dream that, one day, machines are intelligent and accurate enough that mankind is freed from labor entirely. That one day we’ll hit a point of technological advancement that allows most, if not every, necessary function in society and the world to be handled by machines that don’t need to be paid and don’t suffer. And, unlike the above descriptions where this now-freed up manpower can be redirected into some other form of labor, it can now be directed into leisure. I feel that I need to mention that I believe some roles will probably still need a human touch forever. Social issues, perhaps.

The non-financial cost of AI is a hot topic and worth connecting to John Henry as well.

It has been said that the resources consumed by AI damage the planet. AI requires, among other things, electricity, and it is inarguable that many forms of electrical generation harm the planet. Burning coal, for example. And that’s exactly what powered the machine in the tale of John Henry.

We have the benefit of hindsight here. We can observe that over the past centuries that the burning of coal - releasing greenhouse gasses - has done measurable damage to the planet. Damage aside, descriptions of the absolute filth and constant depressingly grey skies of 19th century cities, such as London, boggle the modern mind.

But we can also see that old, harmful technologies such as coal are being replaced by better alternatives. Steam engines gave way to diesel, which perform significantly more work and output less pollution. Even diesel gave way to electric engines, which are even cleaner.

Technology advances. Improvements to the things we want to do - like writing code or laying railways - always come at a cost. There is no free lunch. But those costs decrease over time. We get the same amount of work done given less input. Just look at the advancement of the power efficiency of CPUs or density of hard drives, or the improvement in miles per gallon in cars or even the shift to electric vehicles.

AI has real use, and it’s not going away. It has a cost, and while the level of impact of that cost is hotly debated, it is inarguable that this cost is going to go down over time.

AI feels like a step towards the utopia I described - where all work is taken care of by machines, and humans are free to live as they please and pursue what makes them happy.

This seems like a time to touch on the subject of creativity. A common criticism of AI is that it does not create novel solutions, but is simply an information-laundering operation that - using software engineering for example - steals code from someone else.

And there’s a point to be made there. AI models are in fact created by feeding things created by humans into them. Many opinions, some moral, some legal, exist on the matter. I expect a moment of reckoning will come, like the way it did for Napster.

One version of the tale of John Henry concludes as follows:

Well, they carried John Henry down the tunnel

And they laid his body in the sand.

Now every woman riding on a C and O train

Says, “There lies my steel-driving man, Lord, Lord,

     There lies my steel-driving man.”

In the context of the story, the memory of John Henry isn’t preserved in a monument or a plaque. It’s preserved in folklore. The memory of his deed is remembered by “every woman riding on a C and O train”.

The story’s own image of his legacy is happening on board the very kind of machine he dueled. The railroad won in the sense that it kept running, kept carrying passengers, kept being the dominant mode of transportation.

The craft John Henry dedicated his life to became a footnote of the past, but he wasn’t forgotten by the world. He was preserved, but as folklore riding inside the machine’s success. And it is worth pointing out that the very occupation John Henry was laboring in was itself a form of the advancement of technology: the proliferation of rail-based transportation.

John Henry won his duel, and it didn’t matter. The railroad kept running exactly as it was always going to. This part of the story gets lost when we tell it as a tale of triumph of man over machine. Individual victory and industry-level outcome were never the same contest, and John Henry seems to have believed that winning one settled something about the other.

There’s a version of that same mistake available to us right now. The engineer who refuses to touch AI on principle, be it for quality or moral or resource-related reasons, who wants to out-code the machine to prove that human craft still matters most… I understand that instinct, I’ve felt it myself, and there’s real dignity in it. But it’s a duel, and duels don’t move industries. Winning it, the way John Henry won his, doesn’t change anything.

That’s different from the person who lost their job to automation and is still finding their footing, or the person objecting because their work trained the very model now competing with them. Those aren’t duels for pride, those are real costs and real grievances, and I don’t think they get resolved just because I believe the long arc bends toward less work for everyone. They deserve consideration.

John Henry’s duel itself was a fight to prove something rather than a fight for something. And I think it only delays the utopic fantasy I described earlier. The fantasy, which is the same thing every generation before this one has fought for without knowing it: fewer hours breaking your back, more of them living. Every labor dispute in the story of mechanization was, underneath the immediate fight, an argument about who gets to keep the gains from the machine. My hope is that the endpoint of that argument, run out far enough, is a world with no labor left to dispute over. And so, for the first time, nothing left to exploit either.

None of that arrives on its own, though. The eight-hour work day didn’t show up because factories got generous. People, real human beings, organized and fought for a share of what the machine made possible.

If the same pattern holds here, the utopia I’m describing isn’t something AI hands us automatically just by getting more capable. It’s something we’ll still have to fight for, the same way every generation before us did.

I just don’t think the fight looks like a duel.

sentences.en: The synopsis of the tale of John Henry is as follows:
sentences.zh: 约翰·亨利的故事梗概如下：

blocks.html_en: • John Henry is a railway construction worker and sees a steam-powered machine performing his job at an incredible pace.

sentences.en: John Henry is a railway construction worker and sees a steam-powered machine performing his job at an incredible pace.
sentences.zh: 约翰·亨利是一名铁路建筑工人，他看到一台蒸汽动力机器以令人难以置信的速度完成他的工作。

blocks.html_en: • He decides to measure his prowess as a railway construction worker by having a duel against the steam-powered machine. sentences.en: He decides to measure his prowess as a railway construction worker by having a duel against the steam-powered machine.

blocks.html_en: • John Henry ultimately beats the machine, but the exertion he put his body through to do so causes it to give out, and he passes away.

sentences.en: John Henry ultimately beats the machine, but the exertion he put his body through to do so causes it to give out, and he passes away.
sentences.zh: 约翰·亨利最终击败了机器，但他为此付出的努力导致机器失效，他去世了。

blocks.html_en: It is the classical man-versus-machine tale. And I think the parallels that can be drawn between it and the emergence of AI in recent years are clear, and I will discuss them later on.

sentences.en: It is the classical man-versus-machine tale.
sentences.zh: 这是经典的人与机器的故事。

sentences.en: And I think the parallels that can be drawn between it and the emergence of AI in recent years are clear, and I will discuss them later on.
sentences.zh: 我认为它与近年来人工智能的出现之间的相似之处是显而易见的，我将在稍后讨论它们。

blocks.html_en: I heard the story of John Henry when I was a child, but I forgot all about it until just recently. I subscribe to several different interpretations of the folklore tale, but, in my opinion, it ultimately boils down to a statement on how ever-advancing technology disrupts and conflicts with human dignity, perseverance, ability, and purpose. It is a reasonable conclusion that John Henry felt threatened by the emergence of technology that could replace him. And his response of setting up a duel against said technology suggests that he wanted to prove that he, a human, can equal or defeat the machine. And the outcome of the duel asserts that man, the human spirit, ultimately triumphs over machine, but at a cost. This time, the cost was John Henry’s life.

sentences.en: I heard the story of John Henry when I was a child, but I forgot all about it until just recently.

sentences.en: I subscribe to several different interpretations of the folklore tale, but, in my opinion, it ultimately boils down to a statement on how ever-advancing technology disrupts and conflicts with human dignity, perseverance, ability, and purpose.
sentences.zh: 我同意对这个民间传说故事的几种不同的解释，但在我看来，它最终归结为关于不断进步的技术如何破坏和冲突人类尊严、毅力、能力和目的的陈述。

sentences.zh: 约翰·亨利对可能取代他的技术的出现感到威胁，这是一个合理的结论。

sentences.en: And his response of setting up a duel against said technology suggests that he wanted to prove that he, a human, can equal or defeat the machine.
sentences.zh: 他对与上述技术进行决斗的回应表明，他想证明他，一个人类，可以与机器匹敌或击败机器。

sentences.en: And the outcome of the duel asserts that man, the human spirit, ultimately triumphs over machine, but at a cost.
sentences.zh: 决斗的结果表明，人类、人类精神最终战胜了机器，但也付出了代价。

sentences.en: This time, the cost was John Henry’s life.
sentences.zh: 这一次，代价是约翰·亨利的生命。

blocks.html_en: Looking back on this story almost two centuries later, with a modern perspective over the technology we have now, coaxes out some obviosities. The use of machinery in tunneling and railway construction are the norm. Construction without machinery and with only human labor is practically non-existent anywhere machinery is available. There are still “steel-driving” men, but their tools are no longer hand tools like John Henry’s, but machines.

blocks.html_en: And the benefits of this shift to mechanization are obvious: such projects are completed faster, consuming fewer resources, and - most importantly - more safely and with a lower human cost. Other external factors like safety standards evolving over time too absolutely come into play here. However, having fewer humans on the job site, and more machines, ultimately expose less humans to harm for simple mathematical reasons.

blocks.html_en: Let’s interpret the tale of John Henry in the context of the last couple of years of technological advancement and the emergence and adoption of - and opposition to - AI. I’m a software engineer, and will largely speak from the perspective of my career.

Cherny famously stated that “coding is largely solved” - to the chagrin of many software engineers everywhere.

Yet. I am also not commenting on whether I think AI will ever reach that point. It is inarguable that technology advances and gets better, but it is not a given that all technologies advance and get better. Plenty hit their limit and do not evolve further.

blocks.html_en: Let’s get back to our steam and silicon powered machines.1 Watching the emergence of AI, I have absolutely felt the threat of it, personally. Watching a machine in seconds churn out a Python script that would have taken me at least an hour to write is frightening. Why pay me to spend an hour doing that when a machine can do it instantly? sentences.en: Human code needs review and tweaking, and that doesn’t go away with AI.
sentences.zh: 人类代码需要审查和调整，而这并不会因为人工智能而消失。

sentences.en: Human-written code can still be slop and that slop can get sent to production if it goes unreviewed.
sentences.zh: 人工编写的代码仍然可能是不合格的，如果未经审查，这种不合格的代码可能会被发送到生产环境。

blocks.html_en: These are the two extremes. The far, far ends of the spectrum of AI use. What defines the reasonable middle ground?

sentences.en: These are the two extremes.
sentences.zh: 这是两个极端。

sentences.en: The far, far ends of the spectrum of AI use.
sentences.zh: 人工智能使用范围的最远端。

sentences.en: What defines the reasonable middle ground?
sentences.zh: 什么定义了合理的中间立场？

blocks.html_en: Quality defines the middle ground. A skilled developer can use AI as a force multiplier to write more code at the same quality he would have otherwise, but faster. And that’s what I think a major part of the debate around AI is. What I’ve revealed here is that it all boils down to what one’s viewpoint of the purpose of a human being is.

sentences.en: Quality defines the middle ground.
sentences.zh: 质量决定了中间立场。

sentences.en: A skilled developer can use AI as a force multiplier to write more code at the same quality he would have otherwise, but faster.
sentences.zh: 熟练的开发人员可以使用人工智能作为力量倍增器，以相同的质量编写更多代码，但速度更快。

sentences.en: And that’s what I think a major part of the debate around AI is.
sentences.zh: 我认为这就是围绕人工智能的争论的主要部分。

sentences.en: What I’ve revealed here is that it all boils down to what one’s viewpoint of the purpose of a human being is.
sentences.zh: 我在这里所揭示的是，这一切都归结为一个人对人类目的的看法是什么。

blocks.html_en: Everybody has to work to make the world and society go around. A lot of people think this sucks, and working your entire life is a tragedy. And I’m inclined to agree.

sentences.en: Everybody has to work to make the world and society go around.
sentences.zh: 每个人都必须努力让世界和社会运转。

sentences.en: A lot of people think this sucks, and working your entire life is a tragedy.
sentences.zh: 很多人认为这很糟糕，一生都在工作是一场悲剧。

sentences.en: And I’m inclined to agree.
sentences.zh: 我倾向于同意。

blocks.html_en: But I also see technology as an escape from this existence. In John Henry’s time, digging a tunnel required the toil of thousands of men and women. Or, similarly, farming required hundreds of men or women working the fields, becoming sunburnt and ruining their backs bending down to reach the plants on the ground. These occupations were dangerous and took an extreme toll on the body.

sentences.en: But I also see technology as an escape from this existence.
sentences.zh: 但我也将技术视为逃避现实的一种方式。

sentences.en: In John Henry’s time, digging a tunnel required the toil of thousands of men and women.
sentences.zh: 在约翰·亨利时代，挖掘隧道需要成千上万的男人和女人的辛劳。

sentences.en: Or, similarly, farming required hundreds of men or women working the fields, becoming sunburnt and ruining their backs bending down to reach the plants on the ground.
sentences.zh: 或者，类似地，农业需要数百名男人或女人在田里劳作，他们被晒伤，弯下腰才能够到地上的植物，他们的背部都被晒伤了。

sentences.en: These occupations were dangerous and took an extreme toll on the body.
sentences.zh: 这些职业很危险，对身体造成极大的伤害。

blocks.html_en: But those jobs are done differently now. Farming no longer requires thousands tending the fields year-round, almost all of the work can be done by machine, with one machine replacing many, many workers. Ditto for tunneling.

sentences.en: But those jobs are done differently now.
sentences.zh: 但现在这些工作的完成方式有所不同。

sentences.en: Farming no longer requires thousands tending the fields year-round, almost all of the work can be done by machine, with one machine replacing many, many workers.
sentences.zh: 农业不再需要数千人常年耕田，几乎所有的工作都可以由机器完成，一台机器代替了很多很多工人。

sentences.en: Ditto for tunneling.
sentences.zh: 隧道挖掘也是如此。

blocks.html_en: The men and women that would have been dying or destroying their bodies doing such labor are now doing something else. That something else might not take a similar toll on their body. And that’s a good thing. I’m describing a net reduction human suffering. And I’m describing manpower that has been freed up that can now be put towards something else that improves humanity, like figuring out how to replace jobs that are necessary but incur human suffering with solutions and machines that don’t suffer.

sentences.en: The men and women that would have been dying or destroying their bodies doing such labor are now doing something else.
sentences.zh: 从事这种劳动本来会导致死亡或毁坏自己身体的男男女女现在正在做其他事情。

sentences.en: That something else might not take a similar toll on their body.
sentences.zh: 其他事情可能不会对他们的身体造成类似的伤害。

sentences.en: And that’s a good thing.
sentences.zh: 这是一件好事。

sentences.en: I’m describing a net reduction human suffering.
sentences.zh: 我描述的是人类痛苦的净减少。

sentences.en: And I’m describing manpower that has been freed up that can now be put towards something else that improves humanity, like figuring out how to replace jobs that are necessary but incur human suffering with solutions and machines that don’t suffer.
sentences.zh: 我描述的是已经被释放的人力，现在可以用于改善人类的其他事情，比如弄清楚如何用不遭受痛苦的解决方案和机器来取代那些必要但会给人类带来痛苦的工作。

blocks.html_en: However, it’s worth mentioning that shift doesn’t happen overnight. People out of work because they were replaced by automation can have a hard time finding a new job. Starting over and shifting to a new field of work is often necessary due to the very automation making the job market in a specific field disappear. Some people become poorer. There are immediate and real world consequences worth considering. This is a legitimate grievance.

sentences.en: However, it’s worth mentioning that shift doesn’t happen overnight.
sentences.zh: 然而，值得一提的是，转变不会在一夜之间发生。

sentences.en: People out of work because they were replaced by automation can have a hard time finding a new job.
sentences.zh: 由于被自动化取代而失业的人可能很难找到新工作。

sentences.en: Starting over and shifting to a new field of work is often necessary due to the very automation making the job market in a specific field disappear.
sentences.zh: 由于自动化使得特定领域的就业市场消失，因此通常需要重新开始并转移到新的工作领域。

sentences.en: Some people become poorer.
sentences.zh: 有些人变得更穷。

sentences.en: There are immediate and real world consequences worth considering.
sentences.zh: 有一些直接且现实的后果值得考虑。

sentences.en: This is a legitimate grievance.
sentences.zh: 这是合理的申诉。

blocks.html_en: But, machines replacing humans isn’t inherently a bad thing. It can be beneficial as it frees up labor resources - those humans - and potentially allocates them to fields that advances the knowledge and capabilities and comfort of the human race.

sentences.en: But, machines replacing humans isn’t inherently a bad thing.
sentences.zh: 但是，机器取代人类本质上并不是一件坏事。

sentences.en: It can be beneficial as it frees up labor resources - those humans - and potentially allocates them to fields that advances the knowledge and capabilities and comfort of the human race.
sentences.zh: 它是有益的，因为它释放了劳动力资源（即人类），并有可能将它们分配到提高人类知识、能力和舒适度的领域。

blocks.html_en: And it’s a snowball effect. The observation that technology is advancing at a faster and faster pace is a common one, and accurate in my opinion.

sentences.en: And it’s a snowball effect.
sentences.zh: 这是一个滚雪球效应。

sentences.en: The observation that technology is advancing at a faster and faster pace is a common one, and accurate in my opinion.
sentences.zh: 技术正在以越来越快的速度进步的观察是常见的，并且在我看来是准确的。

blocks.html_en: I dream that, one day, machines are intelligent and accurate enough that mankind is freed from labor entirely. That one day we’ll hit a point of technological advancement that allows most, if not every, necessary function in society and the world to be handled by machines that don’t need to be paid and don’t suffer. And, unlike the above descriptions where this now-freed up manpower can be redirected into some other form of labor, it can now be directed into leisure. I feel that I need to mention that I believe some roles will probably still need a human touch forever. Social issues, perhaps.

sentences.en: I dream that, one day, machines are intelligent and accurate enough that mankind is freed from labor entirely.
sentences.zh: 我梦想有一天，机器足够智能和精确，使人类完全摆脱劳动力。

sentences.en: That one day we’ll hit a point of technological advancement that allows most, if not every, necessary function in society and the world to be handled by machines that don’t need to be paid and don’t suffer.
sentences.zh: 有一天，我们将达到技术进步的一个点，使社会和世界上的大多数（如果不是全部）必要功能都可以由不需要付费且不会遭受痛苦的机器来处理。

sentences.en: And, unlike the above descriptions where this now-freed up manpower can be redirected into some other form of labor, it can now be directed into leisure.
sentences.zh: 而且，与上述描述不同的是，现在释放的人力可以重新投入其他形式的劳动，现在可以将其投入休闲。

sentences.en: I feel that I need to mention that I believe some roles will probably still need a human touch forever.
sentences.zh: 我觉得我需要提一下，我相信有些角色可能仍然需要永远的人情味。

sentences.en: Social issues, perhaps.
sentences.zh: 也许是社会问题。

blocks.html_en: The non-financial cost of AI is a hot topic and worth connecting to John Henry as well.

sentences.en: The non-financial cost of AI is a hot topic and worth connecting to John Henry as well.
sentences.zh: 人工智能的非财务成本是一个热门话题，也值得与约翰·亨利联系。

blocks.html_en: It has been said that the resources consumed by AI damage the planet. AI requires, among other things, electricity, and it is inarguable that many forms of electrical generation harm the planet. Burning coal, for example. And that’s exactly what powered the machine in the tale of John Henry.

sentences.en: It has been said that the resources consumed by AI damage the planet.
sentences.zh: 有人说，人工智能消耗的资源会损害地球。

sentences.en: AI requires, among other things, electricity, and it is inarguable that many forms of electrical generation harm the planet.
sentences.zh: 人工智能除其他外还需要电力，毫无疑问，许多形式的发电都会损害地球。

sentences.en: Burning coal, for example.
sentences.zh: 以烧煤为例。

sentences.en: And that’s exactly what powered the machine in the tale of John Henry.
sentences.zh: 这正是约翰·亨利故事中机器的动力。

blocks.html_en: We have the benefit of hindsight here. We can observe that over the past centuries that the burning of coal - releasing greenhouse gasses - has done measurable damage to the planet. Damage aside, descriptions of the absolute filth and constant depressingly grey skies of 19th century cities, such as London, boggle the modern mind.

sentences.en: We have the benefit of hindsight here.
sentences.zh: 我们在这里有事后诸葛亮的好处。

sentences.en: We can observe that over the past centuries that the burning of coal - releasing greenhouse gasses - has done measurable damage to the planet.
sentences.zh: 我们可以观察到，在过去的几个世纪里，煤炭燃烧（释放温室气体）对地球造成了可衡量的损害。

sentences.en: Damage aside, descriptions of the absolute filth and constant depressingly grey skies of 19th century cities, such as London, boggle the modern mind.
sentences.zh: 撇开损害不谈，对伦敦等 19 世纪城市的绝对肮脏和持续令人沮丧的灰色天空的描述令现代人感到困惑。

blocks.html_en: But we can also see that old, harmful technologies such as coal are being replaced by better alternatives. Steam engines gave way to diesel, which perform significantly more work and output less pollution. Even diesel gave way to electric engines, which are even cleaner.

sentences.en: But we can also see that old, harmful technologies such as coal are being replaced by better alternatives.
sentences.zh: 但我们也可以看到，煤炭等旧的有害技术正在被更好的替代技术所取代。

sentences.en: Steam engines gave way to diesel, which perform significantly more work and output less pollution.
sentences.zh: 蒸汽机让位于柴油机，柴油机的工作量显着增加，产生的污染也更少。

sentences.en: Even diesel gave way to electric engines, which are even cleaner.
sentences.zh: 甚至柴油发动机也被电动发动机所取代，电动发动机更加清洁。

blocks.html_en: Technology advances. Improvements to the things we want to do - like writing code or laying railways - always come at a cost. There is no free lunch. But those costs decrease over time. We get the same amount of work done given less input. Just look at the advancement of the power efficiency of CPUs or density of hard drives, or the improvement in miles per gallon in cars or even the shift to electric vehicles.

sentences.en: Technology advances.
sentences.zh: 技术进步。

sentences.en: Improvements to the things we want to do - like writing code or laying railways - always come at a cost.
sentences.zh: 改进我们想做的事情——比如编写代码或铺设铁路——总是要付出代价的。

sentences.en: There is no free lunch.
sentences.zh: 天下没有免费的午餐。

sentences.en: But those costs decrease over time.
sentences.zh: 但这些成本会随着时间的推移而降低。

sentences.en: We get the same amount of work done given less input.
sentences.zh: 在投入较少的情况下，我们可以完成相同数量的工作。

sentences.en: Just look at the advancement of the power efficiency of CPUs or density of hard drives, or the improvement in miles per gallon in cars or even the shift to electric vehicles.
sentences.zh: 只需看看 CPU 能效的提高或硬盘驱动器密度的提高，或者汽车每加仑行驶里程的提高，甚至转向电动汽车即可。

blocks.html_en: AI has real use, and it’s not going away. It has a cost, and while the level of impact of that cost is hotly debated, it is inarguable that this cost is going to go down over time.

sentences.en: AI has real use, and it’s not going away.
sentences.zh: 人工智能有实际用途，而且不会消失。

sentences.en: It has a cost, and while the level of impact of that cost is hotly debated, it is inarguable that this cost is going to go down over time.
sentences.zh: 它是有成本的，虽然该成本的影响程度存在激烈争论，但毫无疑问，随着时间的推移，这一成本将会下降。

blocks.html_en: AI feels like a step towards the utopia I described - where all work is taken care of by machines, and humans are free to live as they please and pursue what makes them happy.

sentences.en: AI feels like a step towards the utopia I described - where all work is taken care of by machines, and humans are free to live as they please and pursue what makes them happy.
sentences.zh: 人工智能感觉就像是迈向我所描述的乌托邦——所有工作都由机器完成，人类可以自由地生活，追求让自己快乐的事情。

blocks.html_en: This seems like a time to touch on the subject of creativity. A common criticism of AI is that it does not create novel solutions, but is simply an information-laundering operation that - using software engineering for example - steals code from someone else.

sentences.en: This seems like a time to touch on the subject of creativity.
sentences.zh: 现在似乎是讨论创造力这个话题的时候了。

sentences.en: A common criticism of AI is that it does not create novel solutions, but is simply an information-laundering operation that - using software engineering for example - steals code from someone else.
sentences.zh: 对人工智能的一个常见批评是，它并没有创造出新颖的解决方案，而只是一种信息洗钱操作——例如使用软件工程——从其他人那里窃取代码。

blocks.html_en: And there’s a point to be made there. AI models are in fact created by feeding things created by humans into them. Many opinions, some moral, some legal, exist on the matter. I expect a moment of reckoning will come, like the way it did for Napster.

sentences.en: And there’s a point to be made there.
sentences.zh: 这里有一点需要说明。

sentences.en: AI models are in fact created by feeding things created by humans into them.
sentences.zh: 人工智能模型实际上是通过将人类创建的东西输入其中而创建的。

sentences.en: Many opinions, some moral, some legal, exist on the matter.
sentences.zh: 关于这个问题存在许多观点，有些是道德的，有些是法律的。

sentences.en: I expect a moment of reckoning will come, like the way it did for Napster.
sentences.zh: 我预计清算的时刻将会到来，就像 Napster 所做的那样。

blocks.html_en: One version of the tale of John Henry concludes as follows:

sentences.en: One version of the tale of John Henry concludes as follows:
sentences.zh: 约翰·亨利的故事的一个版本的结论如下：

blocks.html_en:
Well, they carried John Henry down the tunnel

And they laid his body in the sand.

Now every woman riding on a C and O train

Says, “There lies my steel-driving man, Lord, Lord,

     There lies my steel-driving man.”

sentences.en: Well, they carried John Henry down the tunnelAnd they laid his body in the sand.Now every woman riding on a C and O trainSays, “There lies my steel-driving man, Lord, Lord, There lies my steel-driving man.”
sentences.zh: 好吧，他们把约翰·亨利抬下隧道，把他的尸体放在沙子里。现在，每个乘坐 C 和 O 火车的女人都说：“那儿躺着我的钢铁驾驶者，主啊，主啊，那儿躺着我的钢铁驾驶者。”

blocks.html_en: Well, they carried John Henry down the tunnel

sentences.en: Well, they carried John Henry down the tunnel
sentences.zh: 好吧，他们把约翰·亨利抬进了隧道

blocks.html_en: And they laid his body in the sand.

sentences.en: And they laid his body in the sand.
sentences.zh: 他们把他的尸体埋在沙子里。

blocks.html_en: Now every woman riding on a C and O train

sentences.en: Now every woman riding on a C and O train
sentences.zh: 现在每个女人都乘坐 C 和 O 火车

blocks.html_en: Says, “There lies my steel-driving man, Lord, Lord,

sentences.en: Says, “There lies my steel-driving man, Lord, Lord,
sentences.zh: 说：“那儿躺着我的钢铁驱动者，主啊，主啊，

blocks.html_en: There lies my steel-driving man.”

sentences.en: There lies my steel-driving man.”
sentences.zh: 那儿躺着我的钢铁驾驶者。”

blocks.html_en: In the context of the story, the memory of John Henry isn’t preserved in a monument or a plaque. It’s preserved in folklore. The memory of his deed is remembered by “every woman riding on a C and O train”.

sentences.en: In the context of the story, the memory of John Henry isn’t preserved in a monument or a plaque.
sentences.zh: 在故事的背景下，约翰·亨利的记忆并没有保存在纪念碑或牌匾中。

sentences.en: It’s preserved in folklore.
sentences.zh: 它被保留在民间传说中。

sentences.en: The memory of his deed is remembered by “every woman riding on a C and O train”.
sentences.zh: 他的事迹被“每一个乘坐 C 和 O 列车的女性”所铭记。

blocks.html_en: The story’s own image of his legacy is happening on board the very kind of machine he dueled. The railroad won in the sense that it kept running, kept carrying passengers, kept being the dominant mode of transportation.

sentences.en: The story’s own image of his legacy is happening on board the very kind of machine he dueled.
sentences.zh: 故事本身所描绘的他的遗产形象就发生在他所对抗的那台机器上。

sentences.en: The railroad won in the sense that it kept running, kept carrying passengers, kept being the dominant mode of transportation.
sentences.zh: 铁路获胜是因为它继续运行，继续载客，继续成为主要的运输方式。

blocks.html_en: The craft John Henry dedicated his life to became a footnote of the past, but he wasn’t forgotten by the world. He was preserved, but as folklore riding inside the machine’s success. And it is worth pointing out that the very occupation John Henry was laboring in was itself a form of the advancement of technology: the proliferation of rail-based transportation.

sentences.en: The craft John Henry dedicated his life to became a footnote of the past, but he wasn’t forgotten by the world.
sentences.zh: 约翰·亨利毕生致力于的工艺成为了过去的注脚，但他并没有被世界遗忘。

sentences.en: He was preserved, but as folklore riding inside the machine’s success.
sentences.zh: 他被保留下来，但作为民间传说，蕴藏在机器的成功之中。

sentences.en: And it is worth pointing out that the very occupation John Henry was laboring in was itself a form of the advancement of technology: the proliferation of rail-based transportation.
sentences.zh: 值得指出的是，约翰·亨利从事的职业本身就是技术进步的一种形式：铁路运输的普及。

blocks.html_en: John Henry won his duel, and it didn’t matter. The railroad kept running exactly as it was always going to. This part of the story gets lost when we tell it as a tale of triumph of man over machine. Individual victory and industry-level outcome were never the same contest, and John Henry seems to have believed that winning one settled something about the other.

sentences.en: John Henry won his duel, and it didn’t matter.
sentences.zh: 约翰·亨利赢得了决斗，但这并不重要。

sentences.en: The railroad kept running exactly as it was always going to.
sentences.zh: 铁路一如既往地继续运行。

sentences.en: This part of the story gets lost when we tell it as a tale of triumph of man over machine.
sentences.zh: 当我们把它当作人战胜机器的故事来讲述时，故事的这一部分就消失了。

sentences.en: Individual victory and industry-level outcome were never the same contest, and John Henry seems to have believed that winning one settled something about the other.
sentences.zh: 个人的胜利和行业层面的结果从来都不是同一场比赛，约翰·亨利似乎相信，赢得一个胜利就可以解决另一个问题。

blocks.html_en: There’s a version of that same mistake available to us right now. The engineer who refuses to touch AI on principle, be it for quality or moral or resource-related reasons, who wants to out-code the machine to prove that human craft still matters most… I understand that instinct, I’ve felt it myself, and there’s real dignity in it. But it’s a duel, and duels don’t move industries. Winning it, the way John Henry won his, doesn’t change anything.

sentences.en: There’s a version of that same mistake available to us right now.
sentences.zh: 我们现在可以使用相同错误的一个版本。

sentences.en: The engineer who refuses to touch AI on principle, be it for quality or moral or resource-related reasons, who wants to out-code the machine to prove that human craft still matters most…
sentences.zh: 原则上拒绝接触人工智能的工程师，无论是出于质量、道德还是资源相关的原因，他们想要超越机器的代码来证明人类技术仍然是最重要的……

sentences.en: I understand that instinct, I’ve felt it myself, and there’s real dignity in it.
sentences.zh: 我理解这种本能，我自己也感受到了，这里面有真正的尊严。

sentences.en: But it’s a duel, and duels don’t move industries.
sentences.zh: 但这是一场决斗，而决斗不会改变行业。

sentences.en: Winning it, the way John Henry won his, doesn’t change anything.
sentences.zh: 赢得它，就像约翰·亨利赢得他的胜利一样，不会改变任何事情。

blocks.html_en: That’s different from the person who lost their job to automation and is still finding their footing, or the person objecting because their work trained the very model now competing with them. Those aren’t duels for pride, those are real costs and real grievances, and I don’t think they get resolved just because I believe the long arc bends toward less work for everyone. content_html_zh:
有一个美国民间故事，讲述的是一个名叫约翰·亨利的人。 它可以追溯到 19 世纪中叶，当时美国正在迅速工业化，蒸汽动力的使用正在兴起…… 嗯，蒸汽。

作为一个民间传说，它有很多不同的变体，但大多数例子都将他描述为一个受雇于铁路建设的人。 他的具体角色通常被描述为“钢铁驱动”人，但这有多种具体形式，例如将钢钻锤入岩石中以挖掘铁路隧道，或锤击将铁轨固定在木枕木上的钉子。 一般来说，约翰·亨利被描述为一位技术精湛且受人尊敬的工人。

网上有很多全文版本，但我会特别参考这个。 约翰·亨利的故事梗概如下：

  • 约翰·亨利是一名铁路建筑工人，他看到一台蒸汽动力机器以令人难以置信的速度完成他的工作。
  • 他决定通过与蒸汽动力机器的决斗来衡量自己作为铁路建筑工人的能力。 决斗通常类似于在铁路隧道中采矿或沿着一段轨道进行比赛，获胜者是最快完成的。
  • 约翰·亨利最终击败了机器，但他为此付出的努力导致机器失效，他去世了。

这是经典的人与机器的故事。 我认为它与近年来人工智能的出现之间的相似之处是显而易见的，我将在稍后讨论它们。

我小时候听过约翰·亨利的故事，但直到最近我才完全忘记。 我同意对这个民间传说故事的几种不同的解释，但在我看来，它最终归结为关于不断进步的技术如何破坏和冲突人类尊严、毅力、能力和目的的陈述。 约翰·亨利对可能取代他的技术的出现感到威胁，这是一个合理的结论。 他对与上述技术进行决斗的回应表明，他想证明他，一个人类，可以与机器匹敌或击败机器。 决斗的结果表明，人类、人类精神最终战胜了机器，但也付出了代价。 这一次，代价是约翰·亨利的生命。

近两个世纪后，以现代视角审视我们现有的技术，回顾这个​​故事，我们会发现一些显而易见的事实。 在隧道挖掘和铁路施工中使用机械是常态。 在有机械的地方，几乎不存在没有机械、仅靠人力的施工。 仍然有“钢铁驱动”的人，但他们的工具不再是约翰·亨利那样的手工工具，而是机器。

这种向机械化转变的好处是显而易见的：此类项目完成得更快，消耗的资源更少，而且最重要的是更安全且人力成本更低。 其他外部因素，例如随着时间的推移而发展的安全标准，也绝对会在这里发挥作用。 然而，由于简单的数学原因，工作现场的人员较少，机器较多，最终会减少受到伤害的人员。

我断言约翰·亨利故事背后的意义直接适用于现在正在发生的事情。 它可以很容易地被解释为一个寓言，描述人工智能的出现以及人工智能的出现对劳动的执行方式以及人类在工作方面的价值的影响。

让我们在过去几年的技术进步以及人工智能的出现和采用（以及反对）的背景下解读约翰·亨利的故事。 我是一名软件工程师，主要从我职业生涯的角度来谈谈。

有人推测软件工程将被人工智能取代。 Boris Cherny 是 Anthropic 的 Claude Code 的创始人和负责人，Anthropic 目前是真正创造人工智能而不是消费人工智能的顶尖公司之一。 切尔尼有句名言：“编码已在很大程度上得到解决”——这让世界各地的许多软件工程师感到懊恼。

这是我们与约翰·亨利的第一个相似之处。 理论上，机器已经被创造出来，可以代替人类并完成以前需要人类完成的任务。 这对应于约翰·亨利所对抗的蒸汽动力机器。

侧边栏：我完全理解，你无法将一个人从办公桌上移开，然后将人工智能放在那里并获得 1:1 的结果。 我并不是说人工智能足够复杂和准确，以至于这是可行的。 我以写代码为生。 我看过AI生成的代码。 他们还不是一个级别的。 然而。 我也不会评论我认为人工智能是否会达到这一点。 毫无疑问，技术不断进步和变得更好，但并不是所有技术都进步和变得更好。 很多都达到了极限并且不再进一步进化。

让我们回到我们的蒸汽和硅动力机器。1 看着人工智能的出现，我个人绝对感受到了它的威胁。 看着一台机器在几秒钟内生成一个需要我至少一个小时才能编写的 Python 脚本，这真是令人恐惧。 当机器可以立即完成这项工作时，为什么要付钱给我花一个小时来做​​呢？ 感觉就像在寻找我的替代者。 我可以想象，近两个世纪前的约翰·亨利在看着蒸汽动力机器完成他的工作时也感到同样的恐惧。

如果我决定与取代我的机器决斗，就像约翰·亨利与他的机器决斗一样，我的故事会是什么样子？

我从 2000 年代中期开始就开始编程，并从 2010 年开始成为专业人士。 我一直关注包括人工智能在内的新兴技术，并寻找可以利用它们成为更好的开发人员的方法。 到目前为止，我已经拥有相当多的使用人工智能工具来执行我的手艺的经验。

话虽如此，我定期查看人工智能工具的输出，发现它通常无法与熟练人类编写的代码相比。 但这并不太令人惊讶。 传达软件项目的需求也经常会让人犯难。 有一个完整的工作领域致力于沟通和跟踪需求——项目管理。 因此，缺乏上下文的机器人输出未达标的代码也就不足为奇了。 最重要的是，人工智能在技术上受到上下文窗口等约束的限制，这些约束很容易导致类似的故障。

但我也认识到法学硕士输出的代码通常“足够好”。 它完成了任务，但采用的模式是我不同意或不知道更好的方法。 有时，没关系。 输出可以作为通用框架，可供人类改进。 它可以做出甚至人类都错过的假设，现在需要考虑。 或者，如果任务足够琐碎，例如一次性任务，“足够好”可能就足够了。

我还需要提到的是，有时人工智能编写的代码与我编写的代码完全一样，这感觉令人惊奇和神奇。

质量对我来说很重要。 我无法强调交付丑陋但有效的代码是多么痛苦。 即使在人工智能的背景之外。 我完全认识到史蒂夫·乔布斯是一个有严重缺陷的人，但我喜欢他与父亲互动的故事，在这个故事中，他的父亲解释了正确、谨慎地完成工作的价值。

约翰·亨利的故事并没有涉及作品的质量或者作品对他是否重要。 但是，他在此事上的立场是可以推断的。 这个故事的版本包括：

他拿起一把锤子和一小块钢，说道：“锤子将是我的死亡，主啊，主啊，锤子将是我的死亡。”

约翰·亨利将一生奉献给了他的手艺。

这就引出了我想要传达的核心内容：

他关心工作本身的工艺和自豪感，而不仅仅是结果。 对于人工智能来说也是如此：如果你关心创造和做事，并且过程比结果更重要，那么人工智能不适合你。

如果你想完成工作，人工智能可以成为力量倍增器。 代码可能不是很好，但它可能会工作。 人类代码需要审查和调整，而这并不会因为人工智能而消失。 人工编写的代码仍然可能是不合格的，如果未经审查，这种不合格的代码可能会被发送到生产环境。

这是两个极端。 人工智能使用范围的最远端。 什么定义了合理的中间立场？

质量决定了中间立场。 熟练的开发人员可以使用人工智能作为力量倍增器，以相同的质量编写更多代码，但速度更快。 我认为这就是围绕人工智能的争论的主要部分。 我在这里所揭示的是，这一切都归结为一个人对人类目的的看法是什么。

每个人都必须努力让世界和社会运转。 很多人认为这很糟糕，一生都在工作是一场悲剧。 我倾向于同意。

但我也将技术视为逃避现实的一种方式。 在约翰·亨利时代，挖掘隧道需要成千上万的男人和女人的辛劳。 或者，类似地，农业需要数百名男人或女人在田里劳作，他们被晒伤，弯下腰才能够到地上的植物，他们的背部都被晒伤了。 这些职业很危险，对身体造成极大的伤害。

但现在这些工作的完成方式有所不同。 农业不再需要数千人常年耕田，几乎所有的工作都可以由机器完成，一台机器代替了很多很多工人。 隧道挖掘也是如此。

从事这种劳动本来会导致死亡或毁坏自己身体的男男女女现在正在做其他事情。 其他事情可能不会对他们的身体造成类似的伤害。 这是一件好事。 我描述的是人类痛苦的净减少。 我描述的是已经被释放的人力，现在可以用于改善人类的其他事情，比如弄清楚如何用不遭受痛苦的解决方案和机器来取代那些必要但会给人类带来痛苦的工作。

然而，值得一提的是，转变不会在一夜之间发生。 由于被自动化取代而失业的人可能很难找到新工作。 由于自动化使得特定领域的就业市场消失，因此通常需要重新开始并转移到新的工作领域。 有些人变得更穷。 有一些直接且现实的后果值得考虑。 这是合理的申诉。

但是，机器取代人类本质上并不是一件坏事。 它是有益的，因为它释放了劳动力资源（即人类），并有可能将它们分配到提高人类知识、能力和舒适度的领域。

这是一个滚雪球效应。 技术正在以越来越快的速度进步的观察是常见的，并且在我看来是准确的。

我梦想有一天，机器足够智能和精确，使人类完全摆脱劳动力。 有一天，我们将达到技术进步的一个点，使社会和世界上的大多数（如果不是全部）必要功能都可以由不需要付费且不会遭受痛苦的机器来处理。 而且，与上述描述不同的是，现在释放的人力可以重新投入其他形式的劳动，现在可以将其投入休闲。 我觉得我需要提一下，我相信有些角色可能仍然需要永远的人情味。 也许是社会问题。

人工智能的非财务成本是一个热门话题，也值得与约翰·亨利联系。

有人说，人工智能消耗的资源会损害地球。 人工智能除其他外还需要电力，毫无疑问，许多形式的发电都会损害地球。 以烧煤为例。 这正是约翰·亨利故事中机器的动力。

我们在这里有事后诸葛亮的好处。 我们可以观察到，在过去的几个世纪里，煤炭燃烧（释放温室气体）对地球造成了可衡量的损害。 撇开损害不谈，对伦敦等 19 世纪城市的绝对肮脏和持续令人沮丧的灰色天空的描述令现代人感到困惑。

但我们也可以看到，煤炭等旧的有害技术正在被更好的替代技术所取代。 蒸汽机让位于柴油机，柴油机的工作量显着增加，产生的污染也更少。 甚至柴油发动机也被电动发动机所取代，电动发动机更加清洁。

技术进步。 改进我们想做的事情——比如编写代码或铺设铁路——总是要付出代价的。 天下没有免费的午餐。 但这些成本会随着时间的推移而降低。 在投入较少的情况下，我们可以完成相同数量的工作。 只需看看 CPU 能效的提高或硬盘驱动器密度的提高，或者汽车每加仑行驶里程的提高，甚至转向电动汽车即可。

人工智能有实际用途，而且不会消失。 它是有成本的，虽然该成本的影响程度存在激烈争论，但毫无疑问，随着时间的推移，这一成本将会下降。

人工智能感觉就像是迈向我所描述的乌托邦——所有工作都由机器完成，人类可以自由地生活，追求让自己快乐的事情。

现在似乎是讨论创造力这个话题的时候了。 对人工智能的一个常见批评是，它并没有创造出新颖的解决方案，而只是一种信息洗钱操作——例如使用软件工程——从其他人那里窃取代码。

这里有一点需要说明。 人工智能模型实际上是通过将人类创建的东西输入其中而创建的。 关于这个问题存在许多观点，有些是道德的，有些是法律的。 我预计清算的时刻将会到来，就像 Napster 所做的那样。

约翰·亨利的故事的一个版本的结论如下：

好吧，他们把约翰·亨利抬下隧道，把他的尸体放在沙子里。现在，每个乘坐 C 和 O 火车的女人都说：“那儿躺着我的钢铁驾驶者，主啊，主啊，那儿躺着我的钢铁驾驶者。”

在故事的背景下，约翰·亨利的记忆并没有保存在纪念碑或牌匾中。 它被保留在民间传说中。 他的事迹被“每一个乘坐 C 和 O 列车的女性”所铭记。

故事本身所描绘的他的遗产形象就发生在他所对抗的那台机器上。 铁路获胜是因为它继续运行，继续载客，继续成为主要的运输方式。

约翰·亨利毕生致力于的工艺成为了过去的注脚，但他并没有被世界遗忘。 他被保留下来，但作为民间传说，蕴藏在机器的成功之中。 值得指出的是，约翰·亨利从事的职业本身就是技术进步的一种形式：铁路运输的普及。

约翰·亨利赢得了决斗，但这并不重要。 铁路一如既往地继续运行。 当我们把它当作人战胜机器的故事来讲述时，故事的这一部分就消失了。 个人的胜利和行业层面的结果从来都不是同一场比赛，约翰·亨利似乎相信，赢得一个胜利就可以解决另一个问题。

我们现在可以使用相同错误的一个版本。 原则上拒绝接触人工智能的工程师，无论是出于质量、道德还是资源相关的原因，他们想要超越机器的代码来证明人类技术仍然是最重要的…… 我理解这种本能，我自己也感受到了，这里面有真正的尊严。 但这是一场决斗，而决斗不会改变行业。 赢得它，就像约翰·亨利赢得他的胜利一样，不会改变任何事情。

这不同于因自动化而失去工作但仍在寻找立足点的人，也不同于那些反对的人，因为他们的工作训练了现在与他们竞争的模型。 这些不是为了骄傲而进行的决斗，而是真正的成本和真正的不满，我认为这些问题不会仅仅因为我相信长弧线会朝着减少每个人的工作而得到解决。 他们值得考虑。

约翰·亨利的决斗本身是为了证明某事而不是为某事而战。 我认为这只会推迟我之前描述的乌托邦幻想。 幻想，是这一代人之前的每一代人在不知不觉中为之奋斗的同一件事：更少的时间让你受伤，更多的时间让你活下去。 机械化故事中的每一次劳资纠纷，在直接的斗争之下，都是关于谁应该从机器中获得收益的争论。 我希望这场争论的终点，只要足够远，就是一个没有劳动力可供争论的世界。 因此，第一次没有什么可以利用的了。

不过，这些都不是自动实现的。 八小时工作制并没有出现，因为工厂变得慷慨了。 人们，真正的人类，组织起来并为分享机器所创造的东西而奋斗。

如果同样的模式在这里成立，那么我所描述的乌托邦并不是人工智能通过变得更强大而自动赋予我们的东西。 这是我们仍然必须为之奋斗的事情，就像我们之前的每一代人所做的那样。

我只是不认为这场战斗看起来像决斗。
